invocation_id.description: Present for invocation failures so callers can fetch history/logs.

reason.description:
Why admission refused or gave up on the request (PLT-4634):
`capacity` | `quota` | `queue_full` | `queue_deadline` |
`circuit_open` | `placement`; or why an asynchronous invocation was
refused (PLT-4639): `backlog` | `queue_full` | `queue_unavailable` |
`object_store_unavailable` | `object_quota` | `input_too_large` |
`not_configured`. Absent for every other error.

oneOf.description: OCI reference pinned to a digest. Accepted but not executable by prototype providers.

reserved.description: Sum of every live reservation (starting, busy, parking, idle, draining).

reuse.description:
Whether environments are reused on this node, and the boot identity
check behind it (PLT-4637). Node-wide; no tenant data.

egress_allow.description:
Destinations a `restricted` revision may open (required for
`restricted`, refused for the other profiles). IPv4 CIDRs only;
special-purpose ranges (private, link-local, metadata, loopback, ...)
are refused.

publish_to_prod.description: When true (default), also point alias `prod` at the revision once Ready.

required_region.description:
Region the revision must run in (e.g. `jp`). Admission rejects the
invocation on a node with another or no region label (PLT-4634).

EgressAllowRequest.description: One allowlist entry of a `restricted` revision.

cidr.description: IPv4 network, e.g. `203.0.113.7/32` (a bare address means `/32`).

EnvironmentCounts.description: Environments by lifecycle, as the admission ledger counts them.

parking.description: Being quiesced on the way into the pool.

promised.description: Granted a pooled environment that has not been taken yet.

starting.description: Booting (reserved from the moment the start was granted).

EnvironmentReuseReport.description: Environment reuse on this node (PLT-4637, docs/metrics.md §boot identity).

boot_id_changed.description:
Later attempts that reported a different boot id for the same
environment. Must stay 0.

boot_id_unreported.description:
Attempts without a guest boot id (no guest kernel, e.g. the process
provider).

first_boots.description:
Attempts that were the first dispatch into their environment and
reported a guest boot id.

mode.description:
`warm_reuse`: pooled environments serve later invocations.
`every_invocation_boots`: the provider or configuration has no warm
stage, so every invocation boots its own environment (the process
provider always).

reason.description: The gate that decided the mode.

same_boot_reuses.description:
Later attempts in the same environment that reported the boot id it
booted with: reuse of the same guest.

idle_ttl_seconds.description:
Idle seconds before a pooled environment may be scaled down.
Default: the gateway's `[pool] idle_ttl_seconds`.

min_ready.description:
Environments kept provisioned while an alias routes the revision
(PLT-4635). 0 (default): scale to zero. Needs environment reuse.

scale_down_cooldown_seconds.description:
No scale-down within this many seconds of a scale-up or activation.
Default: the gateway's `[scaling] scale_down_cooldown_seconds`.

deletion_state.description:
`live` | `deleting` (new invocations refused, in-flight work and
environments still draining) | `deleted` (drained).

alias_generation.description:
Generation of the alias route that chose `revision_id`, resolved once
at `accepted_at` (PLT-4635). An alias switch later never re-points an
accepted invocation.

output.description: Inline result when small enough; `null` otherwise or when not succeeded.

InvokeAsyncResponse.description:
`202 Accepted` of `POST /v1/functions/{id}:invokeAsync` (PLT-4639). Sent
only after the invocation, its input and its outbox event committed.

input_storage.description: `inline` (kept in the ledger) | `object` (kept in the object store).

replayed.description: True when an `Idempotency-Key` matched an earlier acceptance.

revision_id.description:
The revision fixed at acceptance. Every later delivery and retry of
this invocation runs it, whatever the alias points at by then.

status.description:
`accepted` (recorded, not yet in the queue) | `queued` (published) |
later states when an idempotent replay finds it further along.

status_url.description: `GET` this for the invocation (also in the `Location` header).

revision_id.description: Pin a specific revision instead of resolving an alias.

deletion_state.description:
`live` | `deleting` (new invocations refused, in-flight work and
environments still draining) | `deleted` (drained).

alias_generation.description:
Generation of the alias route that chose `revision_id`, resolved once
at `accepted_at` (PLT-4635). An alias switch later never re-points an
accepted invocation.

dropped.description: True when lines were dropped because of retention limits.

NodeInfo.description:
The physical host. Distinct from the number of environments on it: adding
hosts is not something this single-node prototype does.

capacity.description: Configured capacity; a missing dimension is unbounded.

host_scale_out.description: How hosts are added: `not_supported` (single node; scale-out is out of scope).

hosts.description: Hosts behind this gateway. Always 1 in the prototype.

max_concurrency.description: Environments starting or busy at once, node-wide.

per_environment_overhead.description: Added to every environment's reservation (VMM + bridge + host artefacts).

reuse.description: Warm reuse: on or off, measured or not, and why.

ResourceAmounts.description:
CPU / memory / ephemeral storage. In [`NodeInfo::capacity`] a missing
value means the dimension is not bounded by configuration.

ReuseInfo.description:
Whether this gateway reuses (warms) execution environments, and why.

The two flags answer two different questions and neither implies the other
(PLT-4633 review F7):

- `enabled` is what this gateway *does*: both gates are open, so
  environments really are pooled and reused.
- `verified` is a fact about the **provider**: it reports both
  `idle_quiesce` and `idle_resume` as `supported`, which it may only do
  once the pause/resume cycle has been measured on real hardware. It says
  nothing about the `[pool]` configuration, so a gateway with reuse
  switched off can still report `verified: true`.

They are separate on purpose: an operator may switch reuse on for an
`unverified` provider in order to take the measurement
(`[pool] allow_unverified_idle`), and such a run must never be presented as
a warm success. `enabled: true, verified: false` therefore means "reuse is
running so it can be measured", not "warm works here" (PLT-4633 acceptance
4, docs/architecture.md §4).

reason.description:
One sentence naming the gate that decided `enabled`. Always present, on
the enabled and the disabled path alike.

verified.description:
The provider reports both idle capabilities as `supported`, i.e. they
were measured. Independent of whether reuse is switched on.

RevisionCapacityInfo.description: Autoscaler view of one revision of the caller's tenant.

idle_ttl_seconds.description: Idle time before a pooled environment may be scaled down.

oneOf.description:
The last scale decision taken for this revision, kept after it
scaled to zero.

min_ready.description:
Environments kept provisioned while the revision is routed
(`execution.min_ready`, PLT-4635). 0: scales to zero.

route_state.description:
`routed` (an alias points at it) | `unrouted` (pinned invocations
only) | `superseded` (an alias moved away: draining) | `deleting`
(its function is being deleted: draining, new work refused).

scale_down_cooldown_seconds.description: No scale-down within this many seconds of a scale-up or activation.

at_zero.description:
What zero environments does *not* remove: the gateway, its store and
the node keep running and cost what they cost.

default_idle_ttl_seconds.description: Idle TTL of revisions that do not set their own.

default_scale_down_cooldown_seconds.description: Scale-down cooldown of revisions that do not set their own.

drain_timeout_seconds.description:
In-flight invocations of a drained revision still running this long
after the drain started are stopped (`Host.DrainTimeout`).

reconcile_interval_ms.description: How often the scale reconciler runs (idle sweep, min_ready, drains).

warm_pool.description:
Whether this gateway can hold idle (warm) environments at all. When
false every environment ends with its invocation and `min_ready` is
not honoured.

TenantCapacityInfo.description: The caller's own tenant. Other tenants are never listed.

resume_ms.description:
Warm starts only: the environment resume and the readiness check that
followed it. Absent on a cold start, which boots instead.

expected_generation.description: When set, the update only applies if the alias is at this generation.

not_billable.description: Always true in the prototype: numbers are usage facts, not charges.

info.description: Management, invoke, logs and usage API of the Tachyon Serverless prototype. Colon-style action paths (`/v1/functions/{id}:invoke`, `/v1/invocations/{id}:cancel`) are accepted as aliases of the slash forms documented here.
info.title: Tachyon Serverless Gateway

401.description: missing or wrong operator credential (tenant tokens are refused)

get.summary:
`GET /metrics` (PLT-4637, docs/metrics.md). Every tenant's revisions,
queues and environments are on it, so only the `[metrics] bearer_token`
operator credential is accepted — never a tenant token — and without one
configured the route does not exist (404).

200.description: provider preflight ok and new invocations are accepted

503.description: provider not ready, dispatcher fenced, or new invocations refused (see `control_plane`)

get.summary:
Node capacity versus reservations, environments by state, the wait queue,
the start-rate limiter and the caller's own tenant and revisions
(PLT-4634). Other tenants are never listed.

parameters.name: path

200.description: the handler's HTTP response (status, headers and body as returned by the function); x-tachyon-invocation-id header

parameters.description: pin a revision instead of resolving an alias
parameters.name: revision_id

parameters.name: alias

parameters.name: idempotency-key

202.description: accepted and committed (invocation, input and outbox event in one transaction); `Location` and `x-tachyon-invocation-id` headers

409.description: idempotency key reused with another input or bound to a synchronous invocation; function deleted; revision not ready

413.description: input over the payload limit, or `reason` = `input_too_large` (over the inline limit without an object store, or over the object size limit)

503.description: `reason` = `queue_unavailable` | `object_store_unavailable` | `not_configured`, or the ledger / configuration is unavailable (`error_type`)

parameters.description: return entries with a generation above this (default 0: everything)
parameters.name: since

get.summary:
`GET /v1/internal/config?since=<generation>` (PLT-4636): the generation
stamped configuration for data planes. Authenticated with the internal
credential (`[control_plane] internal_token`) as a bearer token, never with
a tenant token; served only by a `combined` gateway that has one
configured (404 otherwise).
